equity.notes: Exchange-adjusted daily close. yfinance history from ~2000.

gold.description: Nippon India ETF Gold Bees — INR-denominated gold ETF (NSE)
gold.notes: Tracks MCX gold prices in INR. Preferred over GC=F (USD) to avoid FX mismatch with INR equity returns. Gold currency policy: GC=F requires explicit USD→INR FX conversion before computing returns; not yet implemented.

bond.description: Nippon India Liquid Bees — INR-denominated liquid-bond / cash-equivalent proxy (NSE)
bond.notes: Liquid/overnight Indian ETF tracking the Nifty Liquid Bond Index. Very low volatility — used as a defensive / cash-equivalent bucket. Has continuous NAV history back to 2009 via yfinance. Limitation: short duration. NOT a sovereign bond, government gilt, or 10-year G-Sec; does not provide long-term duration hedge. A previously used gilt-fund ticker was delisted from yfinance in 2026; LIQUIDBEES.NS is the replacement with continuous history from 2009.

vix.description: India VIX — NSE implied volatility index (preferred)
vix.notes: Preferred VIX for Indian market regime detection. Coverage from ~2008. Explicit fallback: use VIX_FALLBACK constant or override vix_ticker. There is NO silent automatic fallback to CBOE VIX.

irx_yield.description: 13-Week US T-Bill Yield (%) — reference only, NOT a price series
irx_yield.notes: A yield expressed in percent (0–10 range). Must NOT be used as a portfolio price. Retained for reference; was incorrectly used as bond_ticker in Phase 1 draft.

cboe_vix_fallback.description: CBOE VIX — US volatility index (explicit fallback only)
cboe_vix_fallback.notes: Use only when ^INDIAVIX is unavailable and an explicit fallback is required. Must be set via vix_ticker override — never used automatically.

negative_control.assignment: IID uniform Bull/Bear/Crisis at eligible signal closes

specification.vix_policy: omit, matching the existing research suite
specification.timestamp_convention: Each row is a close-to-close return date t (Asia/Kolkata trading date, tz-naive). gross_return(t) is earned by holdings in place before close t; transaction_cost(t) is paid at close t on the trade that fills at close t; a target signalled at close t (data through t) fills at close t+1 and first earns t+1 -> t+2.
